module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 884

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/884](https://www.erdosproblems.com/884)
- [Tao25](https://terrytao.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/erdos-884.pdf)
- [Larsen](https://github.com/Larsen-Daniel/Erdos-884/blob/main/884.pdf)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos884

/--
The sum $\sum_{1 \le i < j \le \tau(n)} \frac{1}{d_j - d_i}$ over all pairs of
divisors $d_i < d_j$ of $n$.
-/
noncomputable abbrev sumDivisorInvPairwiseDifference (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
    ∑ j : Fin n.divisors.card, ∑ i : Fin  j,
    (1 : ℚ) / (Nat.nth (· ∣ n) j - Nat.nth (· ∣ n) i )

/--
The sum $\sum_{1 \le i < \tau(n)} \frac{1}{d_{i + 1} - d_i}$ over consecutive
divisors of $n$.
-/
noncomputable abbrev sumDivisorInvConsecutiveDifference (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
    ∑ i : Fin (n.divisors.card - 1),
    (1 : ℚ) / (Nat.nth (· ∣ n) (i + 1) - Nat.nth (· ∣ n) i)

/--
For a natural number n, let $1 = d_1 < \dotsc < d_{\tau(n)} = n$ denote the divisors of $n$
in increasing order.
Does it hold that
$\sum_{1 \le i < j \le \tau(n)} \frac{1}{d_j - d_i} \ll 1 + \sum_{1 \le i < \tau(n)}
 \frac{1}{d_{i + 1} - d_i}$
for $n \to \infty$, i.e.
$\sum_{1 \le i < j \le \tau(n)} \frac{1}{d_j - d_i} \in O \left( 1 + \sum_{1 \le i < \tau(n)}
 \frac{1}{d_{i + 1} - d_i} \right)$?

This conjecture has been **disproved**:
- In September 2025, Terence Tao gave a conditional _negative_ answer assuming the prime tuples
  conjecture, see `erdos_884_false_of_hardy_littlewood` for this implication.
- Daniel Larsen subsequently gave an unconditional disproof.
-/
def Erdos884Prop : Prop :=
    sumDivisorInvPairwiseDifference ≪ 1 + sumDivisorInvConsecutiveDifference

/--
For a natural number n, let $1 = d_1 < \dotsc < d_{\tau(n)} = n$ denote the divisors of $n$
in increasing order.
Does it hold that
$\sum_{1 \le i < j \le \tau(n)} \frac{1}{d_j - d_i} \ll 1 + \sum_{1 \le i < \tau(n)}
 \frac{1}{d_{i + 1} - d_i}$
for $n \to \infty$, i.e.
$\sum_{1 \le i < j \le \tau(n)} \frac{1}{d_j - d_i} \in O \left( 1 + \sum_{1 \le i < \tau(n)}
 \frac{1}{d_{i + 1} - d_i} \right)$?

This conjecture has been **disproved**:
- In September 2025, Terence Tao gave a conditional _negative_ answer assuming the prime tuples
  conjecture, see `erdos_884_false_of_hardy_littlewood` for this implication.
- Daniel Larsen subsequently gave an
  [unconditional disproof](https://github.com/Larsen-Daniel/Erdos-884/blob/main/884.pdf).

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/884](https://www.erdosproblems.com/884)
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/Jayyhk/erdos-lean/blob/f8a51976fd2e66a52b4928c109fb9ae877a1a507/problems/884/Erdos884.lean"]
theorem erdos_884 :
    answer(False) ↔ Erdos884Prop := by
  sorry

/--
In September 2025, Terence Tao gave a conditional _negative_ answer to Erdős problem 884,
disproving it under the assumption of the *qualitative Hardy–Littlewood prime tuples
conjecture*, see Conjecture 1.1 and Theorem 1.1 of
[Tao25](https://terrytao.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/erdos-884.pdf).

The qualitative conjecture states that for every admissible tuple $(h_1, \dotsc, h_k)$ of
integers, i.e. one which avoids at least one residue class modulo $p$ for every prime $p$,
there are infinitely many natural numbers $n$ such that $n + h_1, \dotsc, n + h_k$ are all
prime. Unlike the full Hardy–Littlewood conjecture, it does not give an asymptotic for the
number of such $n$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_884_false_of_hardy_littlewood
    (hHL : ∀ H : Finset ℤ, (∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ∃ a : ℤ, ∀ h ∈ H, ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ a + h) →
      {n : ℕ | ∀ h ∈ H, Prime ((n : ℤ) + h)}.Infinite) :
    ¬Erdos884Prop := by
  sorry

end Erdos884

reformulations.difference: The source asks for an absolute constant C with Σ_{i<j≤t} 1/(d_j−d_i) ≤ C(1 + Σ_{i<t} 1/(d_{i+1}−d_i)) for every n. `Erdos884Prop` is `sumDivisorInvPairwiseDifference =O[atTop] (1 + sumDivisorInvConsecutiveDifference)`: the bound holds only eventually, for some constant, over all n : ℕ including 0. The divisors are enumerated 0-indexed via `Nat.nth (· ∣ n)` over `Fin n.divisors.card`, and the consecutive sum runs over `Fin (τ(n) - 1)`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Both sums are nonnegative: for n ≠ 0, `Nat.nth (· ∣ n)` is strictly increasing below `n.divisors.card`, and for n = 0, `Nat.divisors 0 = ∅` makes both sums empty. So 1 + g(n) ≥ 1, and each single n has a finite ratio f(n)/(1+g(n)). An eventual bound therefore extends to all n by taking the maximum with the finitely many earlier values of f. Including n = 0 (where f = 0) and allowing any real C changes nothing, since n = 2 already forces C > 0. I proved in Lean `Erdos884Prop ↔ ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ n, sumDivisorInvPairwiseDifference n ≤ C * (1 + sumDivisorInvConsecutiveDifference n)`, and from it `(answer(False) ↔ Erdos884Prop) ↔ ¬∃ C, ∀ n, …`. That is exactly Larsen's Theorem 1.1 (the ratio is unbounded). I also checked that `↑i + 1` is elaborated in ℕ (`Fin.val i + 1`), so there is no Fin wraparound, and that the values at n = 6 (197/60 and 7/3) and n = 12 (24593/3960 and 11/3) match hand computations.

reformulations.difference: Tao's Conjecture 1.1 is stated for admissible tuples (h_1,…,h_k) and asks for infinitely many natural n with every n+h_i a (positive) prime. The Lean hypothesis quantifies over `H : Finset ℤ`. It phrases admissibility as `∀ p prime, ∃ a : ℤ, ∀ h ∈ H, ¬ (p:ℤ) ∣ a + h`, and its conclusion uses `_root_.Prime` in ℤ, which also accepts negative primes: `{n : ℕ | ∀ h ∈ H, Prime ((n:ℤ) + h)}.Infinite`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: (1) A tuple and its underlying set give the same admissibility condition and the same primality conclusion. (2) `¬ p ∣ a + h` for all h ∈ H means H avoids the residue class −a mod p, and −a ranges over all classes. (3) The two sets of n differ by a finite set: once n > Σ_{h∈H} |h|, every n+h is positive, and a positive ℤ-prime is a Nat prime. So one set is infinite iff the other is. I proved (3) in Lean: `{n : ℕ | ∀ h ∈ H, Prime ((n:ℤ)+h)}.Infinite ↔ {n : ℕ | ∀ h ∈ H, ∃ q : ℕ, q.Prime ∧ (n:ℤ)+h = q}.Infinite`. The conclusion `¬Erdos884Prop` is Tao's Theorem 1.1 (ratio unbounded), using the equivalence above.

review.notes:
No defects found. Checks performed:
- #print confirms the elaboration. In the consecutive sum the index is `↑i + 1` computed in ℕ, so there is no Fin wraparound. Differences are taken in ℝ (`Nat.cast` to ℝ), not by truncated ℕ subtraction. `1 + …` is the constant function `(1 : ℕ → ℝ)` plus g. `≪` is parsed as `f ≪ (1 + g)`. `erdos_884` is `False ↔ Erdos884Prop`, i.e. ¬Erdos884Prop, which matches both disproofs.
- Boundary cases: `Nat.divisors 0 = ∅`, so both sums are 0 at n = 0 (even though every number divides 0), and both are 0 at n = 1. Since `0 ∤ n` for n > 0, `Nat.nth (· ∣ n) k` is d_{k+1} for k < τ(n), and every index used stays below τ(n).
- Erdős's original 1998 statement sums over j < τ(n). Tao's footnote 1 calls this a likely typo with no impact. The file follows erdosproblems.com (j ≤ t). The difference is anyway at most 2τ(n)/n = O(1).
- Status: `research solved` + `answer(False)` + a `formal_proof` link matches erdosproblems.com ('DISPROVED (LEAN)') and Tao's database. The linked external proof copies the file's definitions verbatim and proves exactly ¬Erdos884Prop. Compiled against this sandbox's newer Mathlib it fails only through API drift (`setOf`→`Set.ofPred`, changed sieve lemma shapes), not for any mathematical reason; in its own environment it reports only standard axioms.
- Scratch files (all compile): /workspace/review/equiv.lean (equivalence with the source's absolute-constant form), /workspace/review/hl.lean (ℤ-prime vs positive-prime), /workspace/review/scratch.lean and scratch12.lean (values at n = 6 and n = 12).
